state:
Goal `core-path` is reached: all nine `Core\Path` members have their about, three examples, an attack, a bench, a recorded figure in `docs/perf/members.ndjson`, `covers:` markers in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/path.rs`'s `mod tests`, and a card in the plain voice.
`bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Path'` prints `nothing owed` and `0 failed` twice. `bun nv owners --closes core-path`, `bun nv playbook --closes core-path` and `bun nv verify --doc` are green.
The `isAbsolute` attack found a real cost: the member parsed every component of the path to read its root. It now reads three bytes (`begins_at_root`), pinned against the full parse by `is_absolute_agrees_with_the_full_parse`.
Nothing is blocked.

backlog: Indexing an `array<string>` with a `uint` allocates twice per read, and an `int` index allocates nothing (`benches/members/core/Path/isAbsolute.nvs` measured both). It is a latency cost on every such loop. It needs a gap record under `data/gaps/` naming the codegen owner; where array indexing is lowered is *not checked*.
The other eight `Core\Path` benches index with a `uint`, so their recorded allocation counts include those two; re-record them once the indexing cost is fixed (`benches/members/README.md`).
